headline_stat.name: fraction of units phase-locked to theta

stated_limitation: The MRL test is conservative: some units that fail it still show spike-triggered LFP averages above their own shuffle band, so 64% should be read as a lower bound on the fraction of entrained units. Phase is referenced to a single channel per session, so preferred phases are comparable within a session but only approximately across sessions... Cell types were assigned from firing rate and autocorrelogram burstiness because this dandiset does not distribute spike waveforms, so the pyramidal/interneuron labels are putative.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000059 is a canonical Buzsáki-lab hippocampal theta dataset explicitly known-good for theta entrainment, with the added bonus of a septal-cooling causal manipulation.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile from two paired NWB assets, clock alignment verified, curated units only, theta reference channel correctly mapped through the DynamicTableRegion, and speed dropouts handled explicitly.
justification.analysis: Correct circular statistics (MRL, Rayleigh, bias-corrected MRL) with a spike-count-preserving circular-shift null, plus STA, split-half, and a NeMoS Poisson GLM controlling for speed and spike history.
justification.correctness: All headline numbers (64% locked, median MRL 0.073 vs chance 0.025, cooling shift -0.66 Hz) reproduce exactly from the committed unit_stats.csv, are internally consistent, and rest on 483 units with proper controls.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show the effect unambiguously, and honestly include weak/non-locked units as gray negative controls rather than only flattering examples.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate, the write-up frames 64% as a conservative lower bound and names single-channel referencing, putative cell-type labels, and the immobility-contrast caveat, all of which the figures support.
